feature: The lower third caption plate keeps its gradient when its colour is set
summary: The Background well for a Lower third caption now shows the plate's violet to lilac ramp, and opens the colour picker on that gradient. Picking a colour changes the stop you are on, so the plate stays a gradient instead of going one flat colour.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Any recording with speech, captions written (timeline + menu, Captions). Walk: Scripts/playtest/lower-third-plate-keeps-its-gradient-walk.json.

try.do: Before this change: Lower third, Background, any shade. The plate went one flat colour.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick the Captions row, click the Lower third tile, and look at Background in the Text section: the swatch shows the ramp.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the Background swatch: the picker opens on Linear at 120 degrees with Stop 1 picked.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click a darker violet under Shades, then press Escape: the plate's left end darkens and the lilac end stays.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open the picker again, click the right stop on the ramp and pick another colour for the far end.
Press Command-Z: the mock's violet to lilac plate is back in one step.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Is editing one stop at a time the way you expected to tune the plate, or did you want one pick to shift the whole ramp's hue?
Does the small ramp in the Background swatch read as a gradient at panel size?
Should picking Solid in the picker keep the plate's first colour, as it does now, or its last?
Is it right that Radial and Angular are offered for the plate too, or should a caption plate only run straight?
rough: No mock draws the Background well or its picker.
At defaults the plate matches the captions mock's Lower third (linear-gradient 120deg, violet to lilac), as it did before.

Measured bar, frame rendered at the playhead, small patches just inside each end of the plate: untouched plate 15.1 apart (mean channel difference); today's build after a pick 0.0 (both #B385FF); this build after picking a darker shade 76.1 (left #4D09B3, right #AC5BE6). The walk fails if the ends come closer than the untouched plate's.
Both stops are editable, the way the picker edits every gradient in the app (the colour styles shelf); a pick does not shift the hue across the whole ramp.
Changes made in the picker land when you let go, not while dragging, the same as every other caption colour well today.
Once the ramp is changed, the Lower third tile no longer shows as picked, the same as after any other change to the look.
Gradient picker header: a long name now shortens before the stop number does (it read 'Caption backgrou...' and lost 'stop 1'). This also applies to the colour styles shelf's picker.
The walk changes the first stop only; editing the far stop goes through the same shared picker the colour styles shelf uses, but no walk drives it on the caption plate.
